column1: # OCR-BAKEOFF: the bake-off's saved readings scored against the truth set (ocr-bakeoff-score, 2026-10-07), by
# ops/ocrlab/score-bakeoff.py --times <time-reads.sh's times.tsv>. Sample: OCR-SAMPLE-2026-10-04.tsv, 67 pages;
# 65 scored (s01 and s05 hold under 20 scored words, which the harness does not score either). Qwen3.5-9B is
# left out (the owner dropped it after 8 pages).
# MEASURE: `ux-harness --truth`'s visMiss, the same match (the scorer reproduces Vision's on 64 of 67 pages; s01 has
# none, and s41 and s42 print a literal tag, which the scorer strips from readings only: up to 0.6 points). `*_miss` = the page's scored body words
# (contested, figure and handwriting words left out) missing from the reading's word bag, i.e. words wrong and
# missing together; word-weighted over the class. `*_added` = reading words matched by no transcript word, over
# the scored words: a crops reading repeats the crops' overlap (Vision's crops add 16-31% that way), so only a
# figure well above that is a defect (DeepSeek's 0.9-1.1 and Qwen3.5-2B's 0.71 are runaway repetition). Read
# order is not scored. A page a reader could not read (`unread`: the guard killed it twice, at 12,297 MB) counts
# as all missing. `cut` = readings stopped at the token or time limit.
# CLASSES: newspaper by route (11 pages, 24,867 words; read as crops); `old` print = documents before 1985
# (33 pages, 16,688 words); modern (21 pages, 8,718 words). Pages read whole, newspapers as crops.
# SPEED: seconds per read and peak MB (the larger of RSS and footprint) from the job's log, through the guard;
# `crops_s` is over the pages each model was owed crops (whole recall < 0.9), a different set per model. Vision
# was timed here by time-reads.sh (vision-read: revision 3, accurate, language correction) on 34 pages, whole and
# as crops, one process a read (model loading included, as for the models). DeepSeek's and LightOnOCR-4bit's
# speeds are the busy machine's (owner, 2026-10-05) and do NOT count: their quiet re-time was started and dropped
# after 23 minutes without a turn at the machine-wide lock (Archive Suite's VM memory runs held it). It changes
# no pick: DeepSeek is out on words; ocr-bakeoff-bits reads LightOnOCR again and times it there.
# REFERENCES: `vision` = Vision on one plain render (it scales the page down: Briefer's typescript loses half its
# words), `vision.crops` = Vision on the crops, `app-layer@832b7ac` = the app's published text layer
# (TRUTH-RUN-2026-09-30-pages.tsv's layerMiss): old print 1.86%, newspapers 21.8%.
# TOP THREE, by words right on old print and newspapers at a speed this Mac can bear:
#   1. falcon-ocr-bf16 — old 0.23%, newspapers 0.52%, 12 s a page whole, 30 s as crops, peak 4.5 GB.
#   2. lightonocr-2-1b-4bit-1540 — old 0.35%, newspapers 0.77%, 13 s a page on the busy machine, an upper bound
#      that is bearable whatever the quiet figure (the 8-bit builds read 13 s quiet); but crops peak 11.3 GB (the guard
#      stops at 12) and two newspapers ran into repetition (s30, s46: added 1.06 and 0.60).
#   3. chandra-ocr-2-oQ8 — old 0.24%, newspapers 0.47% (the best), 82 s a page whole, 163 s as crops, 8.8 GB. It
#      ran every page under the guard, so this Mac bears it, but slowly: 2.3 hours per 100 pages read whole, so
#      for a whole document it is the OVERNIGHT candidate for the owner's review, and in the day only on the lines
#      Vision misses (ocr-hybrid-proto's arrangement c). Surya, the next best, is not much faster (60 s). No
#      slower reader reads clearly better than Chandra or Falcon, so no other is named.
# REJECTED for third: surya-ocr-2-pkg (4-6 GB, 60 s, but 1.45% on old print, six times Falcon's); qwen3.5-4b-4bit
# and qwen3-vl-8b-4bit (1.5-1.7%); LightOnOCR's 8-bit ocr-soup and base (as good on what they read, but the guard
# killed three of the eleven newspapers at 12 GB). Against the app's layer, Falcon misses 88% fewer words on old
# print and 98% fewer on newspapers. Weights kept: 76,585 MB free, over the 20 GB floor. By route:
# OCR-BAKEOFF-2026-10-07-routes.tsv.
